lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription.  
  
You use Microsoft Intune to manage every Windows 11 device.  
  
You create an attack surface reduction (ASR) policy named Profile1 by using the Attack Surface Reduction Rules profile, and assign Profile1 to all devices.  
  
A user reports that an Adobe Reader plug-in is now blocked.  
  
You need to make sure that the plug-in is unblocked.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Create an Endpoint Privilege Management policy and assign the policy to all the devices.
Add a scope tag to Profile1.
Configure ASR Only Per Rule Exclusions in Profile1.
Create a device compliance policy and assign the policy to all the devices.

questions.explanation:
Intune Attack Surface Reduction Rules profiles support **ASR Only Per Rule Exclusions**, which lets an administrator exclude a specified file or application path from the particular ASR rule that blocks it. This preserves the remaining ASR protections while allowing the Adobe Reader plug-in to run.

**Learn more:** [Configure ASR rules and exclusions - Microsoft Defender for Endpoint](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-configure)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that includes Microsoft Intune and has a user named Admin1.  
  
Admin1 must use the Microsoft Intune admin center to complete the following tasks:  
  
- Create and assign apps and policies to users and devices by using Intune.  
- Create, assign, and delete Windows 365 Cloud PC provisioning policies.  
  
You need to assign the necessary roles to Admin1. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Follow the principle of least privilege.  
- Minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Assign Admin1 the Help Desk Operator role.
Assign Admin1 the Cloud PC Reader role.
Assign Admin1 the Cloud PC Administrator role.
Create a custom Microsoft Entra role and assign the role to Admin1.
Create a custom Intune role and assign the role to Admin1.

questions.explanation:
A custom Intune role can grant Admin1 only the needed permissions to create and assign Intune apps and policies, together with the Windows 365 Cloud PC provisioning-policy permissions to create, assign, and delete those policies. Intune supports custom roles for refined least-privileged access, and Windows 365 custom roles created in the Intune admin center expose the required Provisioning Policies permissions. The built-in Cloud PC Administrator role provides read/write access to all Cloud PC features, which is broader than required, and it does not by itself grant the general Intune app and policy permissions.

**Learn more:** [Role-based access control with Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/fundamentals/role-based-access-control/overview) · [Windows 365 role-based access](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-ca/windows-365/enterprise/role-based-access)

In Microsoft Intune, network location ("Locations") is only offered as a compliance condition for the Android device administrator platform; the Location node/setting does not exist for Windows 10, iOS/iPadOS, or Android Enterprise compliance policies. Since Device2 is the only Android device administrator device, it is the only device that can use a location-based (Location1) compliance policy. Device1 (Windows 10) and Device3 (iOS) have no location-based compliance option. Therefore the answer is Device2 only.

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription containing 100 iOS devices enrolled in Microsoft Intune.  
  
You need to deploy a custom line-of-business (LOB) app to the devices by using Intune.  
  
Which extension should you choose for the app package file?
questions.explanation:
When a required app fails to install, the Intune Management Extension retries a limited number of rapid attempts and then falls back to the Global Re-evaluation Schedule (GRS), which triggers a fresh installation attempt once every 24 hours for a failed/unmapped exit code. So an install that fails on January 1, 2024 is next retried on January 2, 2024. The 5-day, 8-day (weekly) and 31-day options don't correspond to any documented Intune retry interval. Hence the correct answer is January 2, 2024.

**Learn more:** [Troubleshooting app installation issues with Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/mem/intune/app-management/troubleshoot-app-install) · [Win32 app retry interval demystified](https://patchtuesday.com/blog/tech-blog/win32app-retry-interval/)

You use Microsoft Intune for device management.

From the Intune admin center, you create and deploy two Windows app (Win32) apps.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription containing 500 computers running Windows 11. The computers are Microsoft Entra joined and enrolled in Microsoft Intune.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have 25 computers running Windows 10 Pro.

You use Windows Admin Center to remotely manage computers running Windows 10.  
  
When you connect to Windows Admin Center, you receive the message shown in the following exhibit.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783772476281-8mntrug3.png)  
  
You need to stop the message from appearing when you connect to Windows Admin Center. Into which certificate store should you import the certificate?
questions.explanation:
The Trusted Root Certification Authorities store contains the root certificates that Windows trusts. Importing the issuing root certificate—or a self-signed gateway certificate acting as its own root—there establishes trust for the Windows Admin Center HTTPS certificate. A certificate that is expired or not yet valid must additionally be replaced with a currently valid certificate.

**Learn more:** [Update the certificate used by Windows Admin Center](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/manage/windows-admin-center/configure/update-certificate) · [Trusted Root Certification Authorities Certificate Store](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/install/trusted-root-certification-authorities-certificate-store)

questions.question:
Solution: You use the Microsoft Intune Company Portal app.  
  
Does this accomplish the goal?
questions.explanation:
The Microsoft Intune Company Portal app can enroll and register an Android device with an organization, establishing its Microsoft Entra device registration.\
\
**Learn more:** [Overview of device enrollment for Android - Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/user-help/enrollment/benefits-android) · [Enroll Android device with Intune Company Portal - Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/user-help/enrollment/enroll-company-portal-android)

questions.question:
Solution: You use Microsoft Entra Connect.  
  
Does this fulfill the goal?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra Connect is not the mechanism for registering an Android device in Microsoft Entra ID. Android devices are registered by using the Company Portal or Microsoft Authenticator app.\
\
**Learn more:** [Microsoft Entra registered devices](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/devices/concept-device-registration)

questions.question:
Solution: You use the Microsoft Authenticator app.  
  
Does this accomplish the goal?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra registration for Android devices is supported through the Microsoft Authenticator app, so it can register the device in the Microsoft Entra tenant.\
\
**Learn more:** [What are Microsoft Entra registered devices?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/devices/concept-device-registration)

questions.question:
Solution: In the Microsoft Entra admin center, assign User1 the Helpdesk Administrator role.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
BitLocker recovery-key rotation in Intune requires an Intune RBAC role that permits the **Remote tasks/Rotate BitLockerKeys** action, such as Help Desk Operator or Endpoint Security Manager, or an equivalent custom Intune role. The Microsoft Entra Helpdesk Administrator role alone does not grant that Intune remote-action permission.\
\
**Learn more:** [Remote device action: BitLocker key rotation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-management/actions/rotate-bitlocker-keys) · [Encrypt Windows devices with BitLocker using Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-configuration/endpoint-security/encrypt-bitlocker-windows)

questions.question:
Solution: In the Microsoft Intune admin center, assign the Help Desk Operator role to User1.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
The built-in Intune Help Desk Operator RBAC role includes the **Remote tasks** permission to rotate BitLocker recovery keys, allowing its assignees to perform that device action in Intune.\
\
**Learn more:** [Encrypt Windows devices with BitLocker using Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-configuration/endpoint-security/encrypt-bitlocker-windows)

questions.question:
Solution: In the Microsoft Intune admin center, assign the Endpoint Security Manager role to User1.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
The built-in Endpoint Security Manager Intune RBAC role permits the BitLocker key rotation remote action, so a user assigned that role can rotate BitLocker recovery keys for managed Windows devices.\
\
**Learn more:** [Remote device action: BitLocker key rotation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-management/actions/rotate-bitlocker-keys)

questions.question:
Solution: You use the Google Chrome app.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Android devices can be registered with Microsoft Entra ID by using the Microsoft Intune Company Portal or Microsoft Authenticator app. Using Google Chrome alone does not register the device in the tenant.\
\
**Learn more:** [Plan your Microsoft Entra device deployment](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/devices/plan-device-deployment)

questions.question:
Solution: You use Microsoft Entra Connect Sync.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra Connect Sync is used to synchronize on-premises Active Directory identities and supports hybrid join workflows for applicable devices; it does not register Android devices. Android device registration in Microsoft Entra ID is performed through Microsoft Intune Company Portal or the Microsoft Authenticator app.\
\
**Learn more:** [What are Microsoft Entra registered devices?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/devices/concept-device-registration) · [Microsoft Entra Connect Sync: Understand and customize synchronization](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/hybrid/connect/how-to-connect-sync-whatis)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Intune Suite.  
  
You use Microsoft Intune to manage Windows 11 devices.  
  
You create a new policy set named Set and add five device configuration profiles for Windows 10 and later.  
  
You create a device compliance policy named Policy1.  
  
You need to ensure that users assigned the device configuration profiles in Set1 are also always assigned Policy1.  
  
What should you configure?
questions.explanation:
An Intune policy set is a single assignable collection of management objects. Adding Policy1 to Set1's configurations makes the compliance policy part of that collection, so it is deployed with the device configuration profiles whenever the policy set is assigned.

**Learn more:** [Use Policy Sets to Group Collections of Management Objects](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/fundamentals/policy-sets)

You need to ensure that when a Windows device joins the Microsoft Entra tenant, it is automatically enrolled in Microsoft Intune.  
  
What should you configure?

options.text: the Windows Information Protection (WIP) user scope
the Microsoft Entra join and registration settings
the mobile device management (MDM) user scope

questions.explanation:
The Microsoft Intune mobile device management (MDM) user scope enables automatic Intune enrollment for Windows devices when they join or register with Microsoft Entra ID. Configure the scope for all users or the applicable user groups.\
\
**Learn more:** [Enable MDM automatic enrollment for Windows](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-enrollment/windows/enable-automatic-mdm)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription.  
  
You need to ensure that when a Windows device joins the Microsoft Entra tenant, it is automatically enrolled in Microsoft Intune.  
  
What should you configure?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Intune security baselines, including the Microsoft Edge Baseline, apply to supported Windows devices. Windows 11 and Windows 10 are supported, whereas Android and iOS devices are not supported by this baseline profile type.

**Learn more:** [Use security baselines to help secure Windows devices you manage with Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-security/security-baselines/overview)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company uses Microsoft Intune for device management.  
  
You need to ensure that only Android devices using Android work profiles can enroll in Intune.  
  
Which two configurations should you make in the device enrollment restrictions? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: From Platform Settings, set Android device administrator Personally Owned to Block.
From Platform Settings, set Android Enterprise (work profile) to Allow.
From Platform Settings, set Android device administrator Personally Owned to Allow.
From Platform Settings, set Android device administrator to Block.

questions.explanation:
Android Enterprise (work profile) must be allowed so eligible work-profile devices can enroll. Android device administrator is a separate enrollment platform and must be blocked entirely to ensure that enrollment is limited to Android work-profile devices. Microsoft notes that devices supporting Android Enterprise personal work profiles also support Android device administrator, and recommends blocking that platform when device-administrator enrollment is not wanted.

**Learn more:** [Enroll personal devices in Intune with Android Enterprise work profile management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-enrollment/android/setup-personal-work-profile) · [Create device platform restrictions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-enrollment/create-platform-restrictions)

questions.question:
You are creating a device configuration profile in Microsoft Intune.  
  
You must configure particular OMA-URI settings in the profile.  
  
Which profile-type template should you select?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Intune custom device configuration profiles support adding OMA-URI settings, including the OMA-URI path, data type, and associated value.\
\
**Learn more:** [Add custom settings for Windows devices in Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-configuration/templates/configure-custom-settings-windows)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 tenant that uses Microsoft Intune.  
  
You use the Company Portal app to access and install published apps on enrolled devices.  
  
From the Microsoft Intune admin center, you add a Microsoft Store app.  
  
Which two **App information** types are visible in the Company Portal?  
  
> NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
For a Microsoft Store app in Intune, both the Information URL and the Privacy URL are shown in the Company Portal. The Developer and Owner fields are optional app metadata and are not identified as Company Portal-visible fields.\
\
**Learn more:** [Add Microsoft Store Apps to Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/app-management/deployment/add-microsoft-store)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Intune Suite. You use Microsoft Intune for device management.  
  
You have a Windows 11 device named Device1 that is enrolled in Intune. Device1 has been offline for 30 days.  
  
You need to remove Device1 from Intune immediately. The solution must ensure that, if the device checks in again, any apps and data provisioned by Intune are removed. User-installed apps, personal data, and OEM-installed apps must remain.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
For Windows devices, the Intune Delete action immediately removes the device record from Intune and triggers a Retire command. When the device next checks in, Retire removes Intune-managed company apps and associated data while preserving personal data and user-installed or OEM-installed apps.

**Learn more:** [Remote device action: Delete](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-management/actions/delete) · [Remote device action: Retire](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-management/actions/retire)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Windows 11-capable device named Device1 that runs the 64-bit edition of Windows 10 Enterprise and has Microsoft Office 2019 installed.  
  
You have the Windows 11 Enterprise images shown in the following table.

Which image or images can be used to perform an in-place upgrade of Device1?

Windows in-place upgrades use the standard Windows installation media image, not a custom image, because apps in the custom image can conflict with apps already installed on the device. The standard x64 Windows 11 Enterprise image matches Device1’s Windows Enterprise edition and 64-bit architecture. [Windows deployment scenarios — Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/deployment/windows-deployment-scenarios)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You use Microsoft Defender for Endpoint to protect computers running Windows 10.  
  
You need to evaluate differences between the Microsoft Defender for Endpoint configuration and the Microsoft-recommended configuration baseline.  
  
Which tool should you use?

options.text: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint Power BI app

questions.explanation:
The Microsoft Defender for Endpoint Power BI app provides reporting for security configuration assessment data, enabling comparison of endpoint configuration settings with Microsoft-recommended baseline settings and identification of configuration gaps. Microsoft’s Defender for Endpoint baseline assessment capabilities assess configuration compliance against a baseline and expose recommended configuration values.

**Learn more:** [Security baseline assessment methods and properties per device — Microsoft Defender for Endpoint](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/api/export-security-baseline-assessment) · [List configurations in active baseline profiles — Microsoft Defender for Endpoint](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/api/get-security-baselines-assessment-configurations)

You need to enable self-service password reset from the sign-in screen.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription.  
  
All Windows devices are enrolled in Microsoft Intune.  
  
You need to create an app protection policy named Policy1 and apply Policy1 to the devices.  
  
What can you protect by using Policy1?

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure AD tenant called contoso.com.

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Intune Suite. You use Microsoft Intune to manage devices.  
  
You plan to deploy two apps, named App1 and App2, to all Windows devices. App1 must be installed before App2.  
  
From the Intune admin center, you create and deploy two Windows app (Win32) apps.  
  
You need to ensure that App1 is installed before App2 on every device.

questions.explanation:

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a hybrid Azure AD deployment that includes 50 Windows 10 devices. All devices are enrolled in Microsoft Intune.  
  
You find that Group Policy settings take precedence over settings configured in Microsoft Intune policies.  
  
You need to ensure that settings configured in Microsoft Intune override the Group Policy settings.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From Group Policy Management Editor, configure the Computer Configuration settings in the Default Domain Policy.
From the Microsoft Intune admin center, create a custom device profile.
From the Microsoft Intune admin center, create an Administrative Templates device profile.
From Group Policy Management Editor, configure the User Configuration settings in the Default Domain Policy.

questions.explanation:
By default Group Policy (GP) wins over MDM/Intune when the same setting is configured in both. To reverse that precedence you must enable the ControlPolicyConflict/MDMWinsOverGP policy CSP, which is applied only at the device scope via a custom OMA-URI value (./Device/Vendor/MSFT/Policy/Config/ControlPolicyConflict/MDMWinsOverGP = 1). In Intune this requires a custom device configuration profile (option B). An Administrative Templates profile (option C) exposes only ADMX-backed settings and does not include the ControlPolicyConflict CSP, and editing Group Policy (options A and D) would not make Intune win. Therefore create a custom device profile.

**Learn more:** [ControlPolicyConflict Policy CSP (MDMWinsOverGP)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/client-management/mdm/policy-csp-controlpolicyconflict)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a subscription to Microsoft 365.  
  
You have 10 computers running Windows 10 that are enrolled in Microsoft Intune.  
  
You need to deploy the Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise suite to every computer.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From the Microsoft Intune admin center, add an app.
From the Microsoft Intune admin center, create a Windows 10 and later device profile.
From the Microsoft Entra admin center, add an enterprise application.
From the Microsoft Entra admin center, add an app registration.

questions.explanation:

Device profiles configure settings, while Microsoft Entra enterprise applications and app registrations support identity and application integration rather than software deployment.

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription containing a user named User1. User1 has been assigned a Windows 10/11 Enterprise E3 license.  
  
You use Microsoft Intune Suite for device management.  
  
User1 activates the following devices:  
  
- Device1: Windows 11 Enterprise  
- Device2: Windows 10 Enterprise  
- Device3: Windows 11 Enterprise  
  
How many additional devices can User1 activate?
questions.explanation:
A Windows Enterprise E3 license is assigned per user and supports activation on up to five devices. With three devices already activated, User1 has capacity for two more devices.\

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that includes 100 Windows 10 devices enrolled in Microsoft Intune.  
  
You plan to use Endpoint analytics.  
  
You need to create baseline metrics.  
  
What should you do first?
questions.explanation:
Endpoint analytics must be enabled and devices must send telemetry so the service can process and display organization metrics. A custom baseline is created from those current metrics; the regression threshold is configured as part of baseline configuration, after data is available.\

You deploy a new workgroup computer, **Computer1**, running Windows 10.  
  
You need to make sure that Log Analytics can be used to query events from Computer1.  
  
What should you do on Computer1?
questions.explanation:
The Azure Monitor Agent is the component installed on a Windows client to collect configured monitoring data, including Windows events, and send it to a Log Analytics workspace. It uses data collection rules to define the collected data.\
\

options.text: a Windows Configuration Designer provisioning package

questions.explanation:
A Windows Configuration Designer provisioning package can apply an Enterprise edition upgrade to an existing Windows installation, enroll the device in Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD), and add applications, including Microsoft Store apps. Because it configures the current installation instead of reimaging the device, existing user-installed applications are retained while requiring minimal user action to apply the package.

You have a Microsoft 365 subscription, and every device runs Windows 10.  
  
You need to stop users from enrolling devices in the Windows Insider Program.  
  
Which two configurations should you perform in the Microsoft Intune admin center? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: a device restrictions device configuration profile
a Windows 10 and later security baseline
a Windows 10 and later update ring

questions.explanation:
A Windows device restrictions profile can block access to the Windows Insider Program. The same outcome can be enforced with a custom device configuration profile that deploys the applicable Windows Policy CSP, such as `Update/ManagePreviewBuilds`; Microsoft documents this CSP as the replacement for the earlier Insider-build access policy on Windows 10, version 1709 and later. Update rings govern update delivery and selected prerelease channels, rather than serving as a direct block on user enrollment.

**Learn more:** [Assign devices to servicing channels for Windows updates](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/deployment/update/waas-servicing-channels-windows-10-updates) · [System Policy CSP](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/client-management/mdm/policy-csp-System)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your network includes an Active Directory domain named contoso.com. The domain has two computers, named Computer1 and Computer2, that run Windows 10.  
  
On Computer1, you must run the `Invoke-Command` cmdlet to execute several PowerShell commands on Computer2.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: On Computer2, run the Enable-PSRemoting cmdlet.
On Computer2, add Computer1 to the Remote Management Users group.
From Active Directory, configure the Trusted for Delegation setting for the computer account of Computer2.
On Computer1, run the New-PSSession cmdlet.

questions.explanation:
`Enable-PSRemoting` configures Computer2 to receive PowerShell remote commands by starting and configuring WinRM, creating a listener, enabling the required firewall exception, and enabling session configurations. It is required on the computer receiving the commands before `Invoke-Command` can connect to it.

**Learn more:** [Enable-PSRemoting (Microsoft.PowerShell.Core)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.core/enable-psremoting?view=powershell-7.6) · [about_Remote_Requirements](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.core/about/about_remote_requirements?view=powershell-7.5)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Android Enterprise fully managed device named Device1 that is enrolled in Microsoft Intune. Device1 is assigned a device profile.  
  
You plan to manage software updates for Device1 by using Android firmware over-the-air (FOTA). You discover that FOTA is unavailable for Device1.  
  
You need to manage Device1 software updates by using Intune instead.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Intune Suite.  
  
You use Microsoft Intune to deploy and manage Windows devices.  
  
You have 100 devices that belonged to users who left your company.  
  
You need to repurpose the devices for new users by removing all data and applications installed by the previous users. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Deploy a new configuration profile to the devices.
Perform a Windows Autopilot reset on the devices.
Perform an in-place upgrade on the devices.
Perform a clean installation of Windows 11 on the devices.

questions.explanation:
Windows Autopilot Reset prepares an Intune-managed Windows device for reuse by removing user data, settings, and apps, while retaining its Microsoft Entra ID and Intune enrollment. It can be initiated remotely through Intune, avoiding the administrative effort of manually performing clean installations on 100 devices.

**Learn more:** [Remote device action: Autopilot Reset](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-management/actions/autopilot-reset) · [Windows Autopilot Reset](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/autopilot/windows-autopilot-reset)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that includes Microsoft Intune.  
  
For macOS devices, you create an update policy named Policy1 with the following settings:  
  
- **All other updates (OS, built-in apps):** Download and install  
- **Assignments:**  
  - **Included groups:** All Devices  
  
Which two update types can Policy1 download and install? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
The **All other updates** category in a macOS Intune update policy covers operating-system updates and built-in app updates. Critical, firmware, and configuration-file updates are independently configured update categories, so they are not included by this setting.

**Learn more:** [Use Microsoft Intune policies to manage macOS software updates](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-updates/apple/deprecated-mdm-policies-macos)

You install and customize Windows 11 on a reference computer.  
  
You need to capture an image of that reference computer and ensure the image can be deployed to multiple computers.  
  
Which command should be run before capturing the image?
questions.explanation:
Sysprep, using the `/generalize` option, removes unique computer-specific information from the Windows installation so the captured image can be safely deployed to other computers. Microsoft requires generalizing an installation before using it for deployment to a new computer.\
\
**Learn more:** [Sysprep Command-Line Options](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/manufacture/desktop/sysprep-command-line-options?view=windows-11)

options.text: Device1, Device2, Device3, and Device4 only

questions.explanation:
Windows 11 requires a 64-bit operating system, so a 32-bit Windows 10 installation cannot be upgraded in place. Microsoft supports a full upgrade from Windows Pro to Windows Enterprise, but does not support a direct full upgrade from Windows Home to Windows Enterprise. A 64-bit Windows 10 Enterprise device can be upgraded in place to Windows 11 Enterprise.

You create an update rings policy and assign it to all Windows devices.  
  
On November 1, you pause the update rings policy.  
  
All devices stay online.  
  
Without making any further changes to the policy, on what date will the devices next attempt to update?
questions.explanation:
Pausing an Intune update ring blocks assigned devices from receiving feature or quality updates for up to 35 days. When that maximum period expires, the pause automatically ends and devices scan Windows Update for applicable updates. A pause starting November 1 therefore expires on December 6.

**Learn more:** [Manage Windows Update Ring Policies - Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-updates/windows/manage-update-rings)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription.  
  
All devices are enrolled in Microsoft Intune.  
  
You need to ensure that devices which have **not** checked in for 30 days are removed from Intune.  
  
What should you configure in the Microsoft Intune admin center?
questions.explanation:
An Intune device cleanup rule can remove device records that have not checked in for a configured number of days. Its inactivity threshold supports values from 30 through 270 days, so setting it to 30 days cleans up stale device records.\
\
**Learn more:** [Automatically Hide Devices With Cleanup Rules - Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/governance/device-cleanup-rules)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that includes a group named Group1.  
  
You need to ensure that only Group1 members can join devices to the Microsoft Entra tenant.  
  
What should you configure in the Microsoft Entra admin center?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra Device settings contains the **Users may join devices to Microsoft Entra** control. Setting it to the selected scope and specifying Group1 restricts Microsoft Entra device joins to members of that group.\
\
**Learn more:** [Manage devices in Microsoft Entra ID using the Microsoft Entra admin center](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/devices/manage-device-identities)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that includes the devices shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783775833384-ftb5uriq.png)  
  
All devices are enrolled in Microsoft Intune and have Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise installed.  
  
On which devices can the Cloud Policy service for Microsoft 365 be used to manage Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise?
questions.explanation:
The Cloud Policy service for Microsoft 365 supports policy settings for Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise on Windows, iOS, and Android devices. It can enforce policies when users sign in to the apps and does not require a device to be domain joined or otherwise managed. Thus, the Windows 11, Windows 10, Android, and iOS devices are all supported.

**Learn more:** [Overview of Cloud Policy service for Microsoft 365](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365-apps/admin-center/overview-cloud-policy)

questions.question:

You need to deploy Microsoft Office Professional Plus 2019 to the computers by using the Microsoft Office Deployment Tool (ODT).  
  
What should you use to create an ODT customization file?
questions.explanation:
The Office Customization Tool creates the configuration files used with the Office Deployment Tool to deploy customized Click-to-Run Office products. This tool is provided through the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center.\
\

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription and 100 computers running Windows 10.  
  
You need to deploy Microsoft Office Professional Plus 2019 to the computers by using the Microsoft Office Deployment Tool (ODT).  
  
What should you use to create an ODT customization file?

options.text: Change the disk type to Dynamically expanding.
Change the disk format to the VHD.

questions.explanation:
Windows 365 custom images require a Generation 2 image with a default 64-GB OS disk, and the VHD must be fixed-size. Azure does not support VHDX for this upload path, so the existing fixed-size VHDX disk must be converted to VHD format.

**Learn more:** [Device images in Windows 365](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-365/enterprise/device-images) · [Convert custom device images to Generation 2 virtual machines in Windows 365](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-365/enterprise/device-images-convert-generation-2)

questions.question:
Solution: In the Microsoft Entra admin center, you modify the User settings and the Device settings.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Minimum PIN length for Windows Hello for Business is configured through Windows Hello for Business policy settings, such as an Intune tenant-wide enrollment policy or an applicable device policy. Microsoft Entra user settings and general device settings do not configure the PIN-length requirement.\
\
**Learn more:** [Windows Hello for Business policy settings](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/identity-protection/hello-for-business/policy-settings) · [Configure a tenant-wide Windows Hello for Business policy with Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-security/identity-protection/configure-tenant-wide-policy)

questions.question:
Solution: In the Microsoft Entra admin center, you modify the User settings and the Device settings.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Windows Hello for Business PIN requirements at device enrollment must be configured through the tenant-wide Windows Hello for Business enrollment policy, including its Minimum PIN length setting. Automatic MDM enrollment only enrolls the device in Intune when it joins Microsoft Entra ID, and a device restrictions profile does not set the Windows Hello for Business PIN requirement for that join-time prompt.

**Learn more:** [Configure a tenant-wide Windows Hello for Business policy with Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-security/identity-protection/configure-tenant-wide-policy) · [Set up automatic enrollment for Windows devices](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-enrollment/windows/enable-automatic-mdm)

questions.question:
Solution: In the Microsoft Entra admin center, configure automatic mobile device management (MDM) enrollment. In the Microsoft Intune admin center, configure the Windows Hello for Business enrollment options.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Automatic MDM enrollment brings newly joined Windows devices under Intune management, and the tenant-wide Windows Hello for Business enrollment policy supports configuring the minimum PIN length. Setting that value to six makes users create a PIN of at least six characters during Windows Hello provisioning.\
\
**Learn more:** [Configure a tenant-wide Windows Hello for Business policy with Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-security/identity-protection/configure-tenant-wide-policy) · [Windows Hello for Business policy settings](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/identity-protection/hello-for-business/policy-settings)

questions.question:
Solution: Configure **Authentication methods** in the Microsoft Entra admin center.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Windows Hello for Business PIN length is governed by the PIN-complexity policy’s **Minimum PIN length** setting, rather than the Microsoft Entra Authentication methods configuration. Microsoft documents this setting under Windows Hello for Business policy settings, with device and user Policy CSP paths for PIN complexity.\
\
**Learn more:** [Windows Hello for Business policy settings](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/identity-protection/hello-for-business/policy-settings)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that includes 1,000 Windows 11 devices enrolled in Microsoft Intune.  
  
You plan to use Intune to deploy an application named App1 that has multiple installation files.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Prepare the contents of App1 by using the Microsoft Win32 Content Prep Tool.
Upload the contents of App1 to Intune.

questions.explanation:
Intune Win32 app deployment requires the application installation files to be prepared with the Microsoft Win32 Content Prep Tool, which packages them into an `.intunewin` file. That package can then be uploaded and configured in Intune.

**Learn more:** [Prepare Win32 app content for upload](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/app-management/deployment/create-win32-package) · [Add, assign, and monitor a Win32 app](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/app-management/deployment/add-win32)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 Business Standard subscription and 100 Windows 10 Pro devices.  
  
You purchase a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription.  
  
You need to upgrade the Windows 10 Pro devices to Windows 10 Enterprise while minimizing administrative effort.  
  
Which upgrade method should you use?

options.text: a Microsoft Deployment Toolkit (MDT) lite-touch deployment
an in-place upgrade by using Windows installation media

questions.explanation:
Windows subscription activation seamlessly steps up qualifying, supported Windows Pro devices to Windows Enterprise after the applicable Enterprise E5 license is assigned to users. It eliminates the need to deploy Enterprise images or perform manual in-place upgrades, minimizing administrative work.\
\
**Learn more:** [Windows subscription activation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/deployment/windows-subscription-activation)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that includes Microsoft Intune.  
  
You need to deploy a custom app to Android devices. The app uses the APK file format.  
  
Which app type should you choose for the deployment?
questions.explanation:
In Microsoft Intune, an Android custom app delivered from an `.apk` installation file is a line-of-business (LOB) app. The LOB app workflow selects an Android APK as the app package file for deployment.\
\
**Learn more:** [Add apps to Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/app-management/deployment/)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that includes Microsoft Intune.  
  
You need to deploy a custom app to Android devices. The app uses the APK file format.  
  
Which app type should you choose for the deployment?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Endpoint configures AIR automation and remediation levels through device groups. A device group can include Device1 and use the **Semi - require approval for all folders** automation level, which requires approval for remediation actions on all files.

**Learn more:** [Configure automated investigation and remediation capabilities in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/configure-automated-investigations-remediation) · [Create and manage device groups in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-gb/defender-endpoint/machine-groups)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Intune.  
  
You need to ensure that apps can be deployed to Android Enterprise devices.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Configure the Partner device management settings.

questions.explanation:

You need to use Device query to collect information about every device managed through Microsoft Intune.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Onboard the devices to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.
Onboard the devices to Endpoint analytics.
Create a compliance policy for all the devices.

questions.explanation:
Device query is part of Intune Advanced Analytics and returns on-demand device state via KQL. Before a device can be queried, it must be reporting into the Advanced Analytics data platform, which means the device has to be enrolled in Endpoint analytics; this is the enabling prerequisite that must be satisfied first. Onboarding to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (B) provides security telemetry/Advanced Hunting in the Defender portal but is not what enables Intune's Device query, and neither Windows license verification (A) nor a compliance policy (D) has any bearing on the query capability. Community answer keys for this MD-102 item also settle on onboarding to Endpoint analytics.

**Learn more:** [Device query (Intune)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/advanced-analytics/device-query) · [Device query requirement Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-my/answers/questions/5840241/device-query-requirement)

A server named Server1 is accessible through Remote Desktop Services (RDS) by using the RD Gateway.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have 100 computers running Windows 10 that connect to an Azure Log Analytics workspace.  
  
Which three types of data can you collect from the computers by using Log Analytics? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: failure events from the Security log
the list of processes and their execution times

third-party application logs stored as text files

questions.question:

You use Intune to manage devices.  
  
You need to review details of device wipes started through Intune.  
  
Which report should you review?
questions.explanation:
The Device actions report lists requested Intune device actions and their statuses. It includes the action status, initiator, and date/time, which provides the details needed to review wipe actions.\

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Intune Reports](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-management/reports/overview) · [Remote Device Actions - Wipe, Lock, Locate, and More](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-management/actions/)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Intune Suite.  
  
You use Intune to manage devices.  
  
You need to review details of device wipes started through Intune.  
  
Which report should you review?

options.text: a device configuration profile based on the Device features templates
a device configuration profile based on the Device restrictions template

questions.explanation:
An iOS/iPadOS device configuration profile based on the Device restrictions template provides the software-update deferral settings. Configure **Defer software updates** and set **Delay default visibility of software updates** to 30 days; this postpones users’ visibility of released updates and their related notifications.

**Learn more:** [Use Microsoft Intune to manage software updates for supervised iOS/iPadOS devices](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-updates/apple/deprecated-mdm-policies-ios)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that includes a user named User1 and 500 Windows devices enrolled in Microsoft Intune.  
  
You configure an attack surface reduction (ASR) rule and enable it in Warn mode.  
  
User1 downloads a file named file1.exe. When User1 tries to run file1.exe, they receive a prompt stating that the content has been blocked. The user unblocks the content.  
  
How much time passes before the user is prompted again to unblock the content?
questions.explanation:
In ASR Warn mode, a user can select Unblock to bypass the block for 24 hours. When that bypass period ends, the user must unblock the content again.\
\
**Learn more:** [Attack surface reduction (ASR) rules overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/attack-surface-reduction-rules-overview)

questions.question:
You use a Microsoft Intune subscription to manage iOS devices.  
  
You configure a device compliance policy that blocks jailbroken iOS devices.  
  
You need to enable Enhanced jailbreak detection.  
  
What should you configure?
questions.explanation:
Enhanced jailbreak detection is an iOS/iPadOS tenant-wide setting in Intune’s Compliance policy settings. The device compliance policy controls the rule that marks jailbroken devices as noncompliant, while Compliance policy settings control this enhanced detection capability.\
\
**Learn more:** [Device compliance policies in Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-security/compliance/overview)

questions.question:

questions.question:

You plan to use Microsoft Cloud PKI to enable email message signing and encryption.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Create device configuration SCEP certificate profiles.
Create device configuration trusted certificate profiles.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that includes devices enrolled in Microsoft Intune.  
  
You plan to use Device query to obtain on-demand information about the devices’ state. The solution must minimize costs.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Use the Collect diagnostics remote action.
Purchase the Intune Advanced Analytics add-on.
Onboard the devices to Endpoint analytics.

questions.explanation:
Intune Device query (running on-demand KQL queries against a device's live state) is a capability of Intune Advanced Analytics, which is licensed either through the standalone Advanced Analytics add-on or as part of the broader Intune Suite. Since the requirement is to minimize cost, you first purchase the cheaper Advanced Analytics add-on rather than the full Intune Suite. Onboarding devices to Endpoint analytics (option D) is free but does not by itself unlock Device query, which needs the Advanced Analytics license, and the Collect diagnostics remote action is a different feature. Hence purchase the Intune Advanced Analytics add-on.

**Learn more:** [Device query - Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/advanced-analytics/device-query)

questions.question:

questions.question:
You have a computer named Computer1 that is running Windows 11.  
  
A user named User1 intends to use Remote Desktop to connect to Computer1.  
  
You must ensure that User1's device is authenticated before the Remote Desktop connection is established and the sign-in page is displayed.  
  
What should you do on Computer1?

options.text: Configure the Remote Desktop Configuration service

questions.explanation:
Network Level Authentication (NLA) authenticates the user before Remote Desktop establishes a full session. This pre-session authentication reduces unauthorized access and ensures that only clients capable of NLA can proceed to the remote sign-in experience.\
\
**Learn more:** [Enable Remote Desktop on your PC](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/remote/remote-desktop-services/remotepc/remote-desktop-allow-access)

questions.question:

You must ensure that User1's device is authenticated before the Remote Desktop connection is established and the sign-in page is displayed.  
  
What should you do on Computer1?

options.text: Allow Windows Remote Management (WinRM) through the Microsoft Defender firewall.
Add an inbound Microsoft Defender Firewall rule.

questions.explanation:

questions.question:
Your network includes an Active Directory domain containing a user named Admin1. All computers run Windows 10.  
  
You enable Windows PowerShell remoting on the computers.  
  
You need to ensure that Admin1 can establish remote PowerShell connections to the computers. The solution must follow the principle of least privilege.  
  
To which group should you add Admin1?

**Learn more:** [about_Remote_Requirements - PowerShell](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.core/about/about_remote_requirements?view=powershell-7.6)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have computers running Windows 10 that connect to an Azure Log Analytics workspace. The workspace is configured to collect all available events from the Windows event logs.  
  
The computers have the logged events shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783772355352-zrpsix8u.png)  
  
Which events are collected in the Log Analytics workspace?
questions.explanation:
With the legacy Log Analytics agent workspace configuration, all available Windows Event Log collection covers the Application and System event logs. It collects the Application success event and the System information and error events. Security audit events require separate security-event collection configuration, so the Security Audit Success event is not collected by this setting.

**Learn more:** [Log Analytics - Windows security logs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/235333/log-analytics-windows-security-logs) · [Collect Windows events from virtual machines with Azure Monitor Agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/vm/data-collection-windows-events)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft Intune deployment that includes the resources shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783772596234-nh0tm07u.png)  
  
You create a policy set named Set1 and add Comply1 to Set1.  
  
Which additional resources can you add to Set1?
questions.explanation:
Intune policy sets can include device compliance policies and device configuration profiles, and they support Windows and iOS/iPadOS settings in the same policy set. Conditional Access policies and Office app policies are not supported policy-set objects.\
\
**Learn more:** [Use Policy Sets to Group Collections of Management Objects](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/fundamentals/policy-sets)

questions.question:
You have a subscription to Microsoft 365.  
  
Each user has a Windows 365 Enterprise license assigned.  
  
You need to deploy Cloud PCs that will be Microsoft Entra hybrid joined.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Create a configuration profile in Microsoft Intune.

questions.explanation:
A Microsoft Entra hybrid-joined Cloud PC requires an Azure network connection (ANC) with connectivity to the Windows Server Active Directory domain. The provisioning policy must select an ANC for this join type, so the ANC must exist first.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure network connection overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-365/enterprise/azure-network-connections) · [Create provisioning policies for Windows 365](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-365/enterprise/create-provisioning-policy)

questions.question:
You have a subscription to Microsoft 365.  
  
Each user has a Windows 365 Enterprise license assigned.  
  
You need to deploy Cloud PCs that will be Microsoft Entra hybrid joined.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Modify the Data protection settings of Policy1.

questions.explanation:
Intune app protection policy settings apply only to apps managed by that policy; they do not prevent an unmanaged email client from accessing Exchange Online. An app-based Conditional Access policy can require an approved or app-protected client, blocking unmanaged email clients and allowing Microsoft apps such as Outlook to access organizational email.

**Learn more:** [Use app-based Conditional Access policies with Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-security/conditional-access-integration/app-based-policies) · [Conditional Access - Require approved app or app protection policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/policy-all-users-approved-app-or-app-protection)

![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783772592780-4pya0wiq.png)  
  
Which devices can be activated by using subscription activation?
questions.explanation:
Windows subscription activation can step up qualifying Windows Pro devices to Enterprise when the devices are Microsoft Entra joined or hybrid joined. Microsoft Entra registered devices are unsupported. Device1 and Device3 are joined Windows Pro devices, so they qualify.\

**Learn more:** [Windows subscription activation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/deployment/windows-subscription-activation)

options.text: Integrate Intune with Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.
Implement the Mobile Threat Defense connector.
Deploy an attack surface reduction (ASR) policy.
Deploy an Intune security baseline for Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Endpoint integration enables Intune security tasks, which support collaboration on identifying and remediating device vulnerabilities. The integration must be configured before those Defender-originated tasks can be reviewed in the Intune admin center.

**Learn more:** [Manage endpoint security in Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-security/endpoint-security-policies) · [Configure Microsoft Defender for Endpoint with Intune and onboard devices](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-security/microsoft-defender/configure-integration)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription containing 500 computers running Windows 11. The computers are Azure AD joined and enrolled in Microsoft Intune.  
  
You plan to manage Microsoft Defender Antivirus on the computers.  
  
You need to stop users from disabling Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From the Microsoft Intune admin center, create an attack surface reduction (ASR) policy.
From the Microsoft 365 Defender portal, enable tamper protection.
From the Microsoft Intune admin center, create an account protection policy.
From the Microsoft Entra admin center, create a Conditional Access policy.

questions.explanation:
Tamper protection protects Microsoft Defender security settings, including virus and threat protection, from being disabled or changed. In an organization, it can be enabled tenant-wide from the Microsoft Defender portal, preventing individual users from changing the setting.

**Learn more:** [Protect security settings with tamper protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/prevent-changes-to-security-settings-with-tamper-protection) · [Manage tamper protection for your organization using Microsoft Defender portal](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/manage-tamper-protection-microsoft-365-defender)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription.  
  
You plan to enroll 25 new devices in Microsoft Intune.  
  
You need to set up an enrollment notification for the new devices.  
  
Which two notification types can you use? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
> **NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Intune enrollment notifications can be delivered to assigned users by email or as push notifications. These are the supported enrollment-notification delivery methods.\
\
**Learn more:** [Set up enrollment notifications in Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-enrollment/setup-notifications)

You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription and 100 unmanaged iPad devices.  
  
You need to deploy a particular iOS update to the devices. Users must be blocked from manually installing a newer iOS version.  
  
Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Enroll the devices in Microsoft Intune by using the Intune Company Portal.
Create an iOS app provisioning profile.
Enroll the devices in Microsoft Intune by using Apple Business Manager.

questions.explanation:
Intune can deploy a specific available iOS/iPadOS update only to supervised devices. Enrolling through Apple Business Manager provides Automated Device Enrollment and supervision. When a previous or specific update is deployed, a device configuration profile that restricts software-update visibility prevents users from manually installing a newer release.

**Learn more:** [Manage iOS/iPadOS software updates using MDM-based policies in Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-updates/apple/deprecated-mdm-policies-ios)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have 500 computers running Windows 10. The computers are joined to Azure AD and enrolled in Microsoft Intune.  
  
You plan to deploy certificates to the computers by using the Simple Certificate Enrollment Protocol (SCEP).  
  
You have the servers shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783774408538-o8hgfqzs.png)  
  
NDES issues certificates from the subordinate CA.  
  
You are configuring a device configuration profile as shown in the exhibit. (Click the Exhibit tab.)  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783774413354-8g9x9cui.png)  
  
You need to complete the SCEP profile.  
  
On which server is the required root certificate stored?
questions.explanation:
An Intune SCEP profile requires a trusted root CA certificate profile for the issuing CA. Because Server3 is the subordinate CA that issues the certificates through NDES, its trust chain roots at Server2, the root certification authority. Therefore, the required root certificate is on Server2.

**Learn more:** [Configure infrastructure to support SCEP certificate profiles with Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/fundamentals/certificates/scep-infrastructure) · [Trusted root certificate profiles for Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-configuration/certificates/trusted-root-profiles)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 tenant containing the devices shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783773378577-3dweita1.png)  
  
The devices are managed by using Microsoft Intune.  
  
You create a compliance policy named Policy1 and assign Policy1 to Group1. Policy1 is configured to mark a device as Compliant only when its security settings match those specified in the policy.  
  
You discover that devices that are not members of Group1 appear as Compliant.  
  
You need to ensure that only devices assigned a compliance policy can be shown as Compliant. All other devices must appear as Not compliant.  
  
What should you do from the Microsoft Intune admin center?

options.text: From Device compliance, configure the Compliance policy settings.
From Endpoint security, configure the Conditional access settings.
From Tenant administration, modify the Diagnostic settings.
From Policy1, modify the actions for noncompliance.

questions.explanation:
Intune’s tenant-wide Compliance policy settings include the **Mark devices with no compliance policy assigned as** option. Configure it as **Not compliant** so devices without an assigned compliance policy cannot report a Compliant status.

**Learn more:** [Device compliance policies in Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-security/compliance/overview)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft Intune subscription.  
  
Devices are enrolled in Intune as shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783776010537-ogq3hywi.png)  
  
An app named App1 is installed on every device.  
  
What is the minimum number of app configuration policies needed to manage App1?
questions.explanation:
Intune app configuration policies are created for a specific platform. A single policy can cover all applicable Android devices regardless of their Android versions, and another can cover all applicable iOS devices regardless of their iOS versions. Therefore, two policies are required: one for Android and one for iOS/iPadOS.

**Learn more:** [App Configuration Policies for Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/app-management/configuration/overview) · [Add App Configuration Policies for Managed iOS/iPadOS Devices](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/app-management/configuration/configure-managed-ios)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You plan to deploy Windows 11 Pro to 200 new computers by using Microsoft Deployment Toolkit (MDT) and Windows Deployment Services (WDS).  
  
The company has a Volume Licensing Agreement and uses a product key to activate Windows 11.  
  
You must ensure that the new computers are configured with the correct product key during installation.  
  
What should you configure?

options.text: the Device settings in Azure AD

questions.explanation:
An MDT task sequence can specify the Windows product key for the operating-system deployment. MDT supports configuring a Multiple Activation Key (MAK) in the task sequence for Windows deployments under Volume Licensing, and injects that key into the unattended installation configuration.

**Learn more:** [Use the MDT - Configuration Manager](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/configmgr/mdt/use-the-mdt) · [MDT PowerShell Cmdlets: OverrideProductKey](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/configmgr/mdt/mdt-windows-powershell-cmdlets)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription containing 1,000 Windows 11 devices. All devices are enrolled in Microsoft Intune.  
  
You plan to integrate Intune with Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.  
  
You need to create a service-to-service connection between Intune and Defender for Endpoint.  
  
Which settings should you configure in the Microsoft Intune admin center?
questions.explanation:
The Microsoft Defender for Endpoint connector is configured in the Intune admin center under **Tenant administration > Connectors and tokens > Microsoft Defender for Endpoint**. This connection allows Intune to retrieve Defender onboarding information and support Defender for Endpoint integration.\
\
**Learn more:** [Deploy endpoint detection and response policy with Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-configuration/endpoint-security/deploy-edr)

questions.question:
You have a workgroup computer named Client1 that runs Windows 11 and is connected to a public network.  
  
You need to enable PowerShell remoting on Client1. The solution must ensure that PowerShell remoting connections are accepted only from the local subnet.  
  
Which PowerShell command should you run?
questions.explanation:
On Windows client systems connected to a public network, `Enable-PSRemoting -SkipNetworkProfileCheck` enables PowerShell remoting and creates a public-network firewall rule that accepts remote access only from computers in the same local subnet.\
\
**Learn more:** [Enable-PSRemoting (Microsoft.PowerShell.Core)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.core/enable-psremoting?view=powershell-7.5)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription.  
  
You need to grant a user the ability to manage Security defaults and create Conditional Access policies. The solution must follow the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which role should you assign to the user?
questions.explanation:
The Conditional Access Administrator role is the least-privileged role that can configure Security defaults and create or manage Microsoft Entra Conditional Access policies.\
\
**Learn more:** [Configure Security Defaults for Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-in/entra/fundamentals/security-defaults) · [Microsoft Entra built-in roles](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft Deployment Toolkit (MDT) deployment share.  
  
You plan to deploy Windows 11 using the Standard Client Task Sequence template.  
  
You need to modify the task sequence to perform these actions:  
  
- Format disks to support Unified Extensible Firmware Interface (UEFI).  
- Create a recovery partition.  
  
Which task-sequence phase should you modify?
questions.explanation:
MDT performs disk preparation—including creating and formatting target-computer partitions—during the Preinstall phase. The Format and Partition Disk step in that phase can use GPT/EFI partitions for UEFI boot and can define an additional recovery partition.\
\
**Learn more:** [Use the MDT - Configuration Manager](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/configmgr/mdt/use-the-mdt)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription containing 100 devices enrolled in Microsoft Intune.  
  
You need to review the startup processes and the frequency with which each device restarts.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Endpoint analytics provides the Startup performance report, including startup-process impact data and restart-frequency insights for managed devices.\
\
**Learn more:** [Startup Performance Report in Endpoint Analytics - Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/endpoint-analytics/startup-performance)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Intune Suite. You use Microsoft Intune to manage devices.  
  
You need to review device startup times and restart frequencies.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Endpoint analytics provides device-performance insights, including startup times. Its Startup performance report also includes restart-frequency metrics, enabling review of both boot performance and device restart behavior.\
\
**Learn more:** [Startup performance report in Endpoint Analytics](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/analytics/startup-performance) · [Endpoint analytics overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/endpoint-analytics/)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Intune Suite. You use Microsoft Intune to manage devices.  
  
You need to review device startup times and restart frequencies.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
A custom Windows image can be built with the Enterprise edition, App1, and Certificate1 and deployed before Microsoft Entra ID join. Windows Autopilot uses Microsoft Entra join and Intune enrollment to apply device-targeted apps, certificates, and edition configuration. A Windows provisioning package can upgrade the Windows edition, enroll devices in Microsoft Entra ID, install MSI desktop apps, and add certificates. Subscription activation only changes the edition, while an in-place upgrade does not provide the required complete device provisioning workflow.

**Learn more:** [Create a provisioning package (desktop wizard)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/configuration/provisioning-packages/provision-pcs-for-initial-deployment) · [Provision PCs with apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/configuration/provisioning-packages/provision-pcs-with-apps)

questions.question:
You manage 1,000 devices by using Microsoft Intune.  
  
You review the Device compliance trends report.  
  
For what length of time does the report show trend data?
questions.explanation:
The Microsoft Intune Device compliance trends report displays device compliance data over a 30-day trend. The number of devices being managed does not affect that reporting period.\
\
**Learn more:** [Microsoft Intune reports](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-management/reports/overview)

questions.question:
You manage 1,000 devices by using Microsoft Intune.  
  
You review the Device compliance trends report.

options.text: Enable the Allow Remote Shell access setting.
Enable the Allow remote server management through WinRM setting.
Set the Startup Type of the Windows Remote Management (WS-Management) service to Automatic.
Enable the Windows Defender Firewall: Allow inbound Remote Desktop exceptions setting.
Set the Startup Type of the Remote Registry service to Automatic.
Enable the Windows Defender Firewall: Allow inbound remote administration exception setting.

questions.explanation:
WinRM needs its service to start automatically, a WinRM listener to accept remote requests, and a firewall exception for inbound remote-management traffic. The **Allow remote server management through WinRM** policy configures the listener, while the Windows Remote Management (WS-Management) service must be configured for Automatic startup. Microsoft documents that remote management also requires a Windows Firewall exception for WinRM traffic.

**Learn more:** [RemoteManagement Policy CSP — Allow remote server management through WinRM](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/client-management/mdm/policy-csp-remotemanagement) · [Set-WSManQuickConfig](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.wsman.management/set-wsmanquickconfig?view=powershell-7.6)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Intune Suite.  
  
You use Intune to manage all devices.  
  
Users have iOS devices with Microsoft apps installed.  
  
You need to prevent users from cutting, copying, and pasting data between Microsoft Excel and other apps installed on the devices.  
  
What should you configure?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Intune app protection policies apply data-loss-prevention controls to supported iOS apps, including Microsoft Excel. Their data-protection settings can restrict cut, copy, and paste of organizational data between protected apps and other apps.

**Learn more:** [Create and deploy app protection policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/app-management/protection/create-policy) · [iOS/iPadOS app protection policy settings](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/app-management/protection/ref-settings-ios)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company deploys Azure AD, Microsoft 365, Microsoft Intune, and Azure Information Protection.  
  
The company's security policy specifies the following:  
  
- Personal devices are not required to be enrolled in Intune.  
- Users must authenticate with a PIN before accessing corporate email data.  
- Users may use personal iOS and Android devices to access corporate cloud services.  
- Users must be stopped from copying corporate email data to a cloud storage service other than Microsoft OneDrive for Business.  
  
You need to configure a solution that enforces the security policy.  
  
What should you create?

options.text: a device configuration profile from the Microsoft Intune admin center
a data loss prevention (DLP) policy from the Microsoft Purview compliance portal
an insider risk management policy from the Microsoft Purview compliance portal
an app protection policy from the Microsoft Intune admin center

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Intune app protection policies protect organizational data within supported iOS and Android apps without device enrollment. They can require an app PIN to access corporate data and apply data-relocation controls, including limiting where copies of organizational data can be saved, such as allowing OneDrive for Business while blocking other cloud storage services.

**Learn more:** [App Protection Policies Overview - Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/app-management/protection/overview) · [Data Protection Framework Using App Protection Policies - Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/app-management/protection/data-protection-framework)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft Entra tenant containing the devices shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783776021317-li44ohid.png)  
  
On which devices can you deploy Endpoint Privilege Management (EPM)?
questions.explanation:
Endpoint Privilege Management supports eligible Windows devices that are Microsoft Entra joined or Microsoft Entra hybrid joined and are enrolled in Microsoft Intune (or co-managed with Configuration Manager). Only Device1 meets these conditions; Microsoft Entra registration alone is insufficient, and Android devices are unsupported.\
\
**Learn more:** [Plan and prepare for Endpoint Privilege Management deployment](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/epm/deployment-planning)

questions.question:
